correctness.rationale: Each comparable edge maps to an equal or adjacent pair, so the increment of a lift is uniquely in {-1,0,1} even for the four-vertex crown. A nonzero winding requires all 2N increments to have the same unit sign, giving exactly the parity-preserving dihedral automorphisms. Zero winding gives a closed lifted walk with range length <=N, because the walk must go from its minimum to its maximum and return. An independent structural proof of the periodic restriction uses the eventual image: every iterated image is graph-connected and lies in the short arc, hence the stabilized image is an interval. Every vertex of the stabilized image is periodic, and the map restricts to an automorphism of that path, necessarily identity or reversal. A nontrivial reversal preserves crown order only when the endpoint sum is even; it has one fixed center and half the edge length in two-cycles. The two displayed fold constructions are order-preserving on every noncollapsed edge, close at the seam, and fix or reverse exactly their image; their required lengths 2 ell and 4 b do not exceed 2N, including equality. The whole-crown reflection instead fixes two vertices, while rotation by 2r has period N/gcd(N,r). The orbit product for zeta follows formally by counting fixed vertices of each iterate. Independently enumerated all monotone maps by local order-compatible vertex assignments, using stable images to extract cycles: totals 36, 234, 1544, 10030, 64044 for N=2..6, with exact claimed signature sets. In particular it gives a sharp and attained loss in two-cycle multiplicity under collapse, even though a collapsing map can still preserve a maximal fixed arc; these are natural dynamics questions not answered by counting maps or homotopy classes.
